answers.answer: Deal 4 Player cards to each player in a 2-player game, 3 each in a 3-player game, and 2 each in a 4-player game. Exclude the Epidemic cards before dealing. Each pawn starts in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove Epidemic cards and set them aside; starting hands table; matching colored pawns are placed in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Set the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Reveal 3 Infection cards and put 3 matching cubes on each named city; reveal 3 more and put 2 cubes on each; reveal 3 more and put 1 cube on each. Put all 9 revealed cards in the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: “Place the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost ‘2’ space” and specifies the 3/2/1 cube groups, discards all 9 revealed cards, and makes the remainder the Infection Deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemic cards for Introductory, 5 for Standard, and 6 for Heroic. Remove unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into as many face-down piles as Epidemics used, making them as equal in size as possible; shuffle one Epidemic into each pile and stack them with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts, unused-card removal, equal-size piles, one Epidemic shuffled into each, and smaller piles placed on the bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; repetitions are allowed and you may stop early. Action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve any Epidemics, and discard or play Events until within the hand limit; then infect cities. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: “Do up to 4 Actions,” repeat or stop early, action cards go to the Player Discard Pile; phases are draw 2, then Infect Cities; after all phases play passes left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves to a city connected by a white line and costs no card. Direct Flight discards the card for the destination city. Charter Flight discards the card matching the city you are in to move anywhere. Shuttle Flight moves between cities that both have research stations and costs no card. White lines going off one edge of the board wrap to the other edge.
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table gives each movement and card cost; Special Rules says white lines going off an edge wrap to the other edge.

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city to place a research station from the supply there. If all 6 are already built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set the extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Build a Research Station action; Research station limit and “If more than 6 stations supplied” special rule.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes cubes of only one chosen color. For a cured color, it removes all cubes of that color in the city; for an uncured color, it removes 1. Each different color takes a separate action. Return removed cubes to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: “If that disease is cured, return all cubes of that one color”; “Treat each different color with a separate action”; cubes are returned to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color. The station city need not match that color. Existing cubes remain, and new cubes may still be placed until the disease is eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board when it is cured, eradicate it immediately and flip its marker.
answers.evidence: Discover a Cure action and Special Rules: any research station works; existing cubes remain and new cubes may be placed until eradication; if there are no cubes, eradicate immediately.

answers.answer: Normally, give or take the City card matching the city where both players are. Both players must be in that same city and agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge action: matching current-city card, both players in the same city, both agree; recipient exceeding 7 must immediately discard or play an Event.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's own hand to another player in the same city, on either player's turn. This exception does not let another player give an arbitrary nonmatching City card to the Researcher; the summary says it only transfers from the Researcher's hand to the other player's hand.
answers.evidence: Researcher role and Special Rules: may give any City card; exception applies on either player's turn and “does not allow arbitrary nonmatching cards to be given to the Researcher.”

answers.answer: After actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and the players lose; do not reshuffle discards.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: draw the top 2 together; fewer than 2 remaining means loss, with no reshuffle.

answers.answer: Resolve an Epidemic in order: Increase the Infection Rate marker by one space; Infect by drawing the bottom Infection card and placing cubes of its color in the named city; Intensify by shuffling only the Infection Discard Pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. With two cubes already in that city, add one to reach three, then an outbreak occurs and spreads one cube to each connected city, subject to chain-reaction rules. Put the drawn Infection card in the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify. Remove the resolved Epidemic from the game; do not draw a replacement. The summary says to place 3 cubes, unless the disease is eradicated, and to add only enough to reach 3 if the city already has cubes.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards gives Increase/Infect/Intensify, bottom-card draw, discard and reshuffle destination, and no replacement. It says a city with existing cubes gets only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs. Outbreaks describes spread.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards, respectively.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track table: positions/cards are 1–3 = 2, 4–5 = 3, 6–7 = 4; Player Reference table maps 0–6 Epidemics to 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve all three steps of the first Epidemic, then all three steps of the second; Events may be played between them. After drawing, resolve all Epidemics before enforcing the 7-card hand limit. The summary does not specify whether the player can otherwise reduce an over-limit hand between resolving the two Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once: “resolve all 3 steps for the first, then all 3 steps for the second. Events may be played between the two.” Hand Limit: “After drawing Player cards, first resolve all Epidemic cards drawn, then enforce this limit.”

answers.answer: Flip cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, in a quantity equal to the current infection rate. For a non-eradicated disease, place 1 cube of the matching color in the named city; if that city already has 3 of that color, do not place a fourth and trigger an outbreak. For an eradicated disease, place no cube. A cured but non-eradicated disease can still receive cubes. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, infection-rate quantity, one cube, eradicated disease places none, three cubes triggers outbreak, and each card is discarded. Discover a Cure says new cubes may still be placed until eradication.

answers.answer: The initial outbreak advances the Outbreaks marker once and spreads one cube of that color to each connected city. If a connected city already has 3 cubes of that color, a chain-reaction outbreak happens there after the current outbreak resolves and advances the marker again. The first city cannot receive another cube during the chain if it already had an outbreak while resolving that Infection card. Each city can hold up to 3 cubes of each color, so colors have separate caps.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker advances per outbreak; connected cities receive one cube; a connected full city outbreaks after current outbreak; no cubes added to cities already outbreaked in that Infection card; up to 3 of each color.

answers.answer: No. The summary says Event cards cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card, so Airlift cannot move the Quarantine Specialist after the Infection card is drawn but before its outbreak resolves. After that card is resolved, Events may be played at any time, so Airlift can be used before the next Infection card; the Event player chooses its use, and Airlift requires the other pawn's owner's permission. It costs no action, and played Event cards go to the Player Discard Pile. The summary states that the Quarantine Specialist prevents placement and outbreaks in their current city and connected cities. It does not explicitly describe Airlift timing during an ongoing Infect Cities phase beyond the general timing rule.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: playable at any time but “Cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card”; Airlift moves any pawn with permission; player who plays the Event decides use; played Event cards go to Player Discard Pile. Quarantine Specialist prevents placement and outbreaks in current and connected cities.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes one Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. The limit is one stored card, which does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Contingency Planner role: take 1 Event from anywhere in Player Discard Pile as an action, store on Role card (limit 1; not in hand limit), and remove from game when played.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn, with its owner's permission, to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own. For Direct or Charter Flights, discard cards from the Dispatcher's hand; for a Charter Flight, the card matches the moved pawn's departure city. The Dispatcher cannot direct another pawn to Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions, and cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role details specify both movement options, permission, whose hand pays, Charter card city, restriction to movement, and no Operations Expert special move.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. They lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches the 8th outbreak, if they cannot place the required disease cubes because a color's supply is exhausted (during an epidemic, outbreak, or infection), or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after their actions because fewer than 2 remain. The cube-supply loss happens immediately when the required cubes cannot be placed.
answers.evidence: Victory: all 4 cures, diseases need not be eradicated and cubes may remain. Defeat lists 8 outbreaks, insufficient cube supply, and inability to draw 2 cards; Special Rules says cube-supply failure is an immediate loss.
